scene.help: Which view of the desert: a great dead tree before the citadel, the citadel beyond a lone tree, or an empty sea of dunes with the most black sky (the lightest on an OLED).

palette.help: The colour grade: as painted, colder blue, or a blood-dark red sky and moon halo with white sand.

moonSize.help: How large the crescent moon is.

moonGlow.help: How strongly the crescent's halo glows and lights the clouds near it.

sand.help: How bright the white sand is. The default lets lit sand peak around 205-215/255; lower it to save OLED power and wear.

blowing.help: How much sand skims across the dunes and streams off the crests.

motes.help: How many pale motes rise slowly through the night air.

wind.help: How fast the sand and clouds move and how much the trees sway.

depth.help: How much the scene shifts in depth with the cursor. A slow idle drift always continues, even at 0, to protect the panel.

cursorStrength.help: How much sand your cursor lifts and swirls. Click to send a ring of dust rolling across the ground.

reactivity.help: How much bass sends gusts of sand and pulses the moon's halo, and how much treble makes the sand glint.

blackLevel.help: How aggressively dim tones are crushed to true black. Higher keeps more OLED pixels fully off.

fpsLimit.help: Caps the frame rate. 60 is smooth for this slow scene and saves power on a 240 Hz panel; 'Display refresh rate' renders every refresh.

quality.help: Rendering resolution. Lower it on slow PCs. Touching it turns off the automatic adjustment.

diag.help: Shows the scene, audio, frame rate, particle counts and errors on the wallpaper, for troubleshooting.
